description: Team NAIF on top, Rover-to-Rover V2X
summary:
What did we develop?
We developed Project RED-MAC, an interactive 3D WebGL rover simulation and educational platform grounded in peer-reviewed Vehicle-to-Everything (V2X) wireless research from Kuwait University. The project features an autonomous scouting rover (piloted by the N.A.I.F.-NASA mascot, Colonel Cluck) managing dynamic RF spectrum switching, obstacle diffraction, and sample collection on the Martian surface.

How does it address the challenge?
Direct Earth-to-Mars teleoperation is impossible due to a crippling 6–44 minute light-time delay. RED-MAC solves this through local surface V2X teleoperation between rovers and a Habitat base station. Implementing our "Cruise Low, Transmit High" doctrine, rovers navigate harsh terrain using diffraction-resilient 900 MHz/BPSK to conserve power and avoid dust attenuation, then upshift to 28 GHz mmWave/64-QAM in clear line-of-sight to burst-upload high-bandwidth 4K video and geological payloads to Earth.

Why is it important?
By translating empirical desert research into an interplanetary context, RED-MAC demonstrates that autonomous vehicles cannot rely on a single wireless band. The simulation proves the necessity of adaptive, multi-band architectures advancing both future Mars sample return missions and resilient terrestrial smart city infrastructure.
